st:vegetables-staples-l3.sourceEnglishBody:
A staple earns its place because it feeds the household beyond the day of harvest.

It carries energy or protein. It stores, or it stays in the ground until you need it. And often it carries cultural memory too.

One staple leaves you vulnerable. Two or more give you options when weather or pests hit.

Grow at least two. Not one.

Which staple does your household rely on most heavily right now? That's the one whose failure would hurt most — so that's the one that needs a companion.

Each staple protects you against something different.

Maize gives calories, and stores dry. Open-pollinated maize also lets you save your own seed, if you manage isolation and selection.

Beans and cowpeas give a storable protein harvest.

Sweet potato develops some drought tolerance after its storage roots form. It needs water in the first weeks and while roots are forming; water stress then can reduce the harvest. Its young leaves are edible too.

Amadumbe handles wetter ground, where other staples struggle.

Notice that they fail in different conditions. That's the whole point.

Resilience doesn't mean nothing fails.

It means one failure doesn't finish your household's food plan.

One crop is one point of failure.

Two or more staples give you more ways to keep eating.

Different crops use water, soil and seasons differently. That difference is the protection.
st:vegetables-staples-l3.currentNativeBody:
Staple e tshwanelwa ke sebaka sa yona hobane e fepa lelapa le kamora letsatsi la kotulo.

E fana ka energy kapa protein. E a bolokwa, kapa e sala e le mobung ho fihlela o e hloka. Hangata e boetse e na le cultural memory.

Staple e le nngwe e o siya o sa sireletseha. Tse pedi kapa ho feta di o fa dikgetho ha weather kapa pests di otla.

Lema bonyane tse pedi. E seng se le seng.

Ke staple efe eo lelapa la hao le itšetlehileng ka eona haholo hona joale? That's the one whose failure would hurt most — so that's the one that needs a companion.

Staple e nngwe le e nngwe e o sireletsa kgahlanong le ntho e fapaneng.

Maize e fana ka calories, ’me e ka bolokoa e omme. Open-pollinated maize e boetse e u lumella ho boloka peo ea hao, haeba u laola isolation le selection.

Beans le cowpeas li fana ka protein harvest e ka bolokoang.

Sweet potato e ba le drought tolerance e itseng ka mor’a hore storage roots tsa eona li bopehe. E hloka metsi libekeng tsa pele le ha storage roots li ntse li bopeha; water stress ka nako eo e ka fokotsa harvest. Its young leaves are edible too.

Amadumbe e khona ho mamella wetter ground, moo lijalo tse ling tsa staple li thatafalloang teng.

Hlokomela hore di hloleha maemong a fapaneng. Ke yona ntlha yohle.

Ho mamella maemo a thata ha ho bolele hore ha ho letho le hlolehang.

Ho bolela hore ho hloleha ho le hong ha ho fedise morero wa dijo wa lelapa la hao.

Sejalo se le seng ke point of failure e le nngwe.

Dijalo tse pedi kapa ho feta tsa staple di o fa ditsela tse ngata tsa ho tswela pele o ja.

Dijalo tse fapaneng di sebedisa water, soil le seasons ka ditsela tse fapaneng. Phapang eo ke yona protection.

ve:vegetables-staples-l3.currentNativeBody:
Tshiḽiwa tsha vhuthogwa [staple] tshi wana vhuimo hatsho ngauri tshi ṋea muṱa zwiḽiwa u fhirisa ḓuvha ḽa khaṋo.

Tshiḽiwa tsha vhuthogwa tshi fara energy kana protein. Tshi a vhulungea kana tshi sala tshi mavuni u swika ni tshi tshi ṱoḓa. Nahone kanzhi tshi na cultural memory.

Tshiḽiwa tshithihi tsha vhuthogwa tshi ni sia ni vulnerable. Zwiḽiwa zwa vhuthogwa zwivhili kana zwo engaho zwi ni ṋea khetho musi mutsho kana zwikhokhonono zwi tshi kwama zwimela.

Alusani zwivhili kana zwo engaho. Hu si tshithihi.

Ndi tshiḽiwa tsha vhuthogwa tshifhio tshine muṱa waṋu wa ḓitika ngatsho nga maanḓa u fhira zwiṅwe zwino? That's the one whose failure would hurt most — so that's the one that needs a companion.

Tshiḽiwa tsha vhuthogwa tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe tshi ni tsireledza kha zwithu zwo fhambanaho.

Maize i ṋea calories nahone i a vhulungea yo oma. Open-pollinated maize i dovha ya ni tendela ni vhulunga mbeu yaṋu, arali ni tshi langula isolation na selection.

Beans na cowpeas zwi ṋea protein harvest ine ya nga vhulungwa.

Sweet potato i wana drought tolerance nyana nga murahu ha musi storage roots dza yo dzo no vhumbea. I ṱoḓa maḓi kha vhege dza u thoma na musi storage roots dzi tshi kha ḓi vhumbea; water stress nga tshifhinga tshenetsho i nga fhungudza harvest. Its young leaves are edible too.

Amadumbe i a konḓelela mavu ane a vha na maḓi manzhi u fhira, hune zwiṅwe zwimela zwa vhuthogwa zwa konḓelwa.

Ṱhogomelani uri zwi kundwa kha conditions dzo fhambanaho. Ndi zwone zwine zwa vha ndeme nga maanḓa.

Resilience a zwi ambi uri a hu na zwine zwa kundwa.

Zwi amba uri u kundwa huṅwe huthihi a hu fhedzi pulane ya zwiḽiwa ya muṱa waṋu.

Tshibyariwa tshithihi ndi point nthihi ya failure.

Zwiḽiwa zwa vhuthogwa zwivhili kana zwo engaho zwi ni ṋea dziṅwe nḓila nnzhi dza u bvela phanḓa ni tshiḽa.

Zwimela zwo fhambanaho zwi shumisa maḓi, mavu na khalaṅwaha nga nḓila dzo fhambanaho. Phambano yeneyo ndi yone tsireledzo.

st:vegetables-staples-l4.sourceEnglishBody:
Pest pressure usually rises for a reason.

Plants under stress. One crop dominating the ground. Or broad chemical use that has already removed the predators that were helping you.

So before you treat anything, look at the whole system.

Is the plant short of water? Is the soil compacted, or hungry? Are predators already working on the problem for you?

A yellow leaf is not automatically an insect. It can be water, nutrition, or root damage. Find out which before you act.

Work through four steps, in order.

One. Observe. Look at the damage pattern, the underside of the leaf, the stem, and the plants nearby.

Two. Check for stress. Soil moisture, roots, spacing, nutrition, drainage.

Three. Protect what's helping you. Beneficial insects are doing work you'd otherwise do yourself.

Four. Only then, act — and start with the lightest thing that works. Physical removal, barriers or changes in crop care may help. Check that the action suits the problem and monitor the result.

If a treatment is needed, use a product registered for that crop and pest, and follow its label. This includes neem products. Check protection and harvest waiting instructions. Do not improvise mixtures or stronger doses.

Be honest with yourself about which step you usually skip.
st:vegetables-staples-l4.currentNativeBody:
Pest pressure hangata e a eketseha ka lebaka le itseng.

Dimela tse nang le stress. Sejalo se le seng se laolang sebaka. Kapa broad chemical use e seng e tlositse predators tse neng di o thusa.

Ka hona, pele o phekola eng kapa eng, sheba system yohle.

Na semela se haellwa ke metsi? Na mobu o petetsane kapa ha o na phepo e lekaneng? Na dibatana tsa disenyi di se di thusa ho rarolla bothata?

Lekhasi le lesehla ha le bolele ka boyona hore ho na le disenyi. Bothata e ka ba metsi, phepo ya semela kapa tshenyo ya metso. Fumana hore na ke efe pele o nka kgato.

Sebetsa ka mehato e mene, ka tatellano.

Ntlha ya pele: Sheba. Sheba mokgwa oo tshenyo e hlahang ka wona, bokatlase ba lekhasi, kutu le dimela tse haufinyane.

Ntlha ya bobedi: Lekola dintho tse bakang kgatello semeleng: mongobo wa mobu, metso, sebaka pakeng tsa dimela, phepo le phallo ya metsi.

Ntlha ya boraro: Sireletsa se o thusang. Beneficial insects (likokoanyana tse molemo) li etsa mosebetsi oo u neng u tla o etsa ka bouena.

Ntlha ya bone. Ke ka morao feela moo o nkang kgato — qala ka the lightest thing that works. Physical removal, barriers kapa diphetoho tlhokomelong ya dijalo di ka thusa. Netefatsa hore ketso e loketse bothata, mme o behe leihlo sephethong.

Ha treatment e hlokahala, sebedisa product registered for that crop and pest, mme o latele label ya yona. Sena se kenyeletsa neem products. Hlahloba protection and harvest waiting instructions. Do not improvise mixtures or stronger doses.

Ipolelle nnete, hore na ke mohato ofe oo hangata o o tlolang.

ve:vegetables-staples-l4.sourceEnglishBody:
Pest pressure usually rises for a reason.

Plants under stress. One crop dominating the ground. Or broad chemical use that has already removed the predators that were helping you.

So before you treat anything, look at the whole system.

Is the plant short of water? Is the soil compacted, or hungry? Are predators already working on the problem for you?

A yellow leaf is not automatically an insect. It can be water, nutrition, or root damage. Find out which before you act.

Work through four steps, in order.

One. Observe. Look at the damage pattern, the underside of the leaf, the stem, and the plants nearby.

Two. Check for stress. Soil moisture, roots, spacing, nutrition, drainage.

Three. Protect what's helping you. Beneficial insects are doing work you'd otherwise do yourself.

Four. Only then, act — and start with the lightest thing that works. Physical removal, barriers or changes in crop care may help. Check that the action suits the problem and monitor the result.

If a treatment is needed, use a product registered for that crop and pest, and follow its label. This includes neem products. Check protection and harvest waiting instructions. Do not improvise mixtures or stronger doses.

Be honest with yourself about which step you usually skip.
ve:vegetables-staples-l4.currentNativeBody:
Pest pressure i anzela u engedzea nga tshiitisi.

Zwimela zwi re na stress. One crop dominating the ground. Kana broad chemical use yo no bvisa predators dze dza vha dzi tshi ni thusa.

Ngazwenezwo, ni sa athu u thoma u lafha tshithu, sedzani system yoṱhe.

Naa tshimela tshi khou shaya maḓi? Mavu o compacted kana a si na pfushi? Predators dzi khou shuma kha thaidzo iyi dzi tshi ni thusa already naa?

Yellow leaf a i ambi automatically uri ndi insect. Zwenezwo zwi nga vha maḓi, nutrition, kana u vhaisala ha midzi. Wanani uri ndi zwifhio ni sa athu dzhia vhukando.

Tevhelani vhukando vhuṋa nga u tevhekana.

Tsha u thoma. Sedzani. Sedzani damage pattern, tlhelo ḽa fhasi ḽa ḽiṱari, tsinde, na zwimela zwi re tsini.

Tsha vhuvhili. Sedzani stress. Soil moisture, midzi, spacing ya zwimela, nutrition na drainage.

Tsha vhuraru. Tsireledzani zwine zwa khou ni thusa. Beneficial insects (zwikhokhonono zwine zwa thusa) zwi khou ni itela mushumo une na inwi na vha ni tshi ḓo u ita.

Tsha vhuṋa. Ndi hone fhedzi ni tshi dzhia vhukando — thomani nga the lightest thing that works. Physical removal, barriers kana tshanduko kha nḓila ya u ṱhogomela zwimela zwi nga thusa. Ṱolani arali vhukando vhu tshi tea thaidzo, ni bvele phanḓa ni tshi sedza mvelelo.

Arali treatment i tshi ṱoḓea, shumisani product registered for that crop and pest, nahone ni tevhele label yayo. Hezwi zwi katela neem products. Ṱolani protection and harvest waiting instructions. Do not improvise mixtures or stronger doses.

Ni ḓi ambele ngoho nga ha vhukando vhune na anzela u vhu pfuka.

ts:vegetables-staples-l4.currentNativeBody:
Pest pressure hi ntolovelo yi engetseka hi xivangelo.

Swibyariwa leswi nga na stress. Xibyariwa xin’we lexi lawulaka ndhawu. Kumbe broad chemical use leyi se yi suseke predators leti a ti ku pfuna.

Kutani, loko u nga si tshungula xin'wana ni xin'wana, languta system hinkwawu.

Xana xibyariwa xi pfumala mati? Misava yi compacted kumbe yi pfumala swakudya? Xana predators se ti ku pfuna hi ku tirha eka xiphiqo lexi?

A yellow leaf a swi vuli automatically leswaku ku ni insect. Xivangelo xi nga va mati, nutrition, kumbe ku onhaka ka timitsu. Kuma leswaku i yini u nga si teka goza.

Tirha hi magoza ya mune, hi ku landzelelana.

Xo sungula. Languta pattern ya ku onhaka, tlhelo ra le hansi ra tluka, tsinde, ni swibyariwa leswi nga ekusuhi.

Vumbirhi. Kambela stress. Ndzhongo wa misava, timitsu, mpfhuka wa swimilani, nutrition na drainage.

Vunharhu. Sirhelela leswi swi ku pfunaka. Beneficial insects (switsotswana leswi pfunaka) swi endla ntirho lowu wena a wu ta wu endla hi wexe.

Vumune. Hi kona ntsena u tekaka goza — sungula hi the lightest thing that works. Physical removal, barriers kumbe ku cinca ndlela yo hlayisa swibyariwa swi nga pfuna. Kambela leswaku goza ri fambisana ni xiphiqo, kutani u ya mahlweni u kambela vuyelo.

Loko treatment yi laveka, tirhisa product registered for that crop and pest, kutani u landzelela label ya yona. Leswi swi katsa neem products. Kambela protection and harvest waiting instructions. Do not improvise mixtures or stronger doses.

Tshembeka eka wena n'winyi mayelana na goza leri u talaka ku ri tlula.
